summary: Guided by a star, wise men from the East find the young Child Jesus in Bethlehem, worship Him and give Him gifts, while King Herod plots against Him.
key_insight: In Matthew, the title “King of the Jews” is spoken only by Gentiles: the wise men here, and later Pilate, the soldiers and the sign over the cross. Foreigners worship Jesus by the title for which He will die.
story: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of Herod the king, wise men from the East came to Jerusalem. They asked, “Where is He who has been born King of the Jews? For we have seen His star in the East and have come to worship Him.”

When Herod the king heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. He gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people and asked them where the Christ was to be born. They answered, “In Bethlehem of Judea,” and quoted the prophet: “For out of you shall come a Ruler Who will shepherd My people Israel.”

Then Herod called the wise men secretly and found out from them exactly when the star had appeared. He sent them to Bethlehem with a request: “Go and search carefully for the young Child, and when you have found Him, bring back word to me, that I may come and worship Him also.”

They set out, and the star they had seen in the East went before them, until it came and stood over the place where the young Child was. When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.

They came into the house and saw the young Child with Mary His mother, and they fell down and worshiped Him. Then they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Warned by God in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their own country by another way.

scene.label: Wise men
scene.text: Matthew’s word is magi, the name for a class of priestly scholars in Persia and Babylon who studied the stars and interpreted dreams. Matthew does not say how many came. The number three was later drawn from the three gifts, and the idea that they were kings came later still.

scene.label: Herod the king
scene.text: Herod the Great was an Idumean whom Rome had made king of the Jews. He rebuilt the temple, and he killed anyone he saw as a rival, including his wife Mariamne and three of his own sons. He died in 4 BC, so Jesus was born before then.

scene.label: Bethlehem and a house
scene.text: Bethlehem, David’s hometown, lay about six miles south of Jerusalem, and Micah 5:2 had named it. By now the family was living in a house, and Matthew calls Jesus a “young Child,” not a newborn. Herod’s later order about boys “two years old and under” (Matthew 2:16) suggests that months had passed since the birth.

scene.label: The star
scene.text: Matthew does not explain it. Some suggest an unusual alignment of planets or a comet, but this star “went before them” and stood over one place, which sounds like more than an ordinary star. Long before, Balaam, a seer from the East, had said, “A Star shall come out of Jacob” (Numbers 24:17).

scene.label: The gifts
scene.text: Gold was a gift fit for a king. Frankincense was burned in worship. Myrrh was a costly spice used in anointing and in burial (John 19:39). Isaiah 60:6 pictures the nations coming to Israel’s light: “They shall bring gold and incense.”

witnesses.matthew: Matthew alone tells of the wise men. His Gospel presents Jesus as the promised King, and here the King is sought by Gentiles from far away while Jerusalem’s king and its Bible scholars stay where they are. The Gospel that ends with “make disciples of all the nations” (Matthew 28:19) begins with the nations coming to worship.

seeing.reveals: Jesus is the Ruler and Shepherd Micah promised, the true King of the Jews, and He is worthy of worship even as a small child in an ordinary house.
seeing.living: The chief priests and scribes knew exactly where the Christ would be born, and Matthew does not say that one of them walked the six miles to see Him. Knowing the right answers about Jesus is not the same as coming to Him. The wise men traveled far, rejoiced, bowed down and opened their treasures.
seeing.ponder: Do you know about Jesus the way the scribes did, or have you come into the house, bowed before Him and opened your treasures to Him?

preaching.big_idea: The King of the Jews draws worshipers from far away, while those nearest Him stay home.
outline: Joy at the end of the search (9–10)
preaching.watch_for: Matthew 2 is built around places, each tied to Scripture: Bethlehem (2:6), Egypt (2:15), Ramah (2:18) and Nazareth (2:23). Matthew shows where the Messiah came from and why, one place at a time.
